france24fr.title: Crash d'un débris de fusée SpaceX sur la Lune : petit impact, grandes ambitions
france24fr.description: L'étage supérieur de la fusée Falcon 9 de SpaceX lancée en janvier 2025 s'est écrasé sur la Lune mercredi. france24fr.description: La propagation de contenus hostiles sur les réseaux sociaux en Malaisie a aggravé les tensions envers la communauté de réfugiés rohingyas, entraînant l’expulsion d'un village de plus de 100 personnes et la fermeture temporaire d’écoles accueillant des enfants réfugiés.

france24fr.description: Longtemps cantonnés à la science-fiction, les robots humanoïdes sont désormais l'un des secteurs les plus convoités de la Silicon Valley. spiegel.title: Türkei und PKK: Parlament bringt eingeschränkte Amnestie für PKK-Kämpfer auf den Weg
spiegel.description: Die Türkei arbeitet an einem rechtlichen Rahmen für den Umgang mit ehemaligen Mitgliedern der PKK. Tausende Häftlinge könnten davon profitieren, doch eine Freilassung des Anführers Abdullah Öcalan ist ausgeschlossen.

spiegel.title: Flughafen Leipzig/Halle: Die Drohne war eine fliegende Bombe
spiegel.description: Hochexplosiver Sprengstoff, dazu ein Zünder: Der Flughafen Leipzig entging womöglich nur durch Glück einem Anschlag. Innenminister Alexander Dobrindt spricht von einer »neuen Gefahrenqualität«. Steckt Russland dahinter?

spiegel.title: Bangladesch: Sheikh Hasina will trotz drohender Todesstrafe heimkehren
spiegel.description: Obwohl ihr die Todesstrafe droht, möchte die frühere Ministerpräsidentin Sheikh Hasina in diesem Jahr aus Indien nach Bangladesch zurückkehren. Sie sagt, sie fürchte keine Festnahme.

spiegel.title: BMW: Spider-Man-Werbung auf Autodisplay nervt Fahrer
spiegel.description: Noch vor wenigen Jahren versprach der BMW-Infotainment-Chef, keine Werbung in Autos abspielen zu wollen. Nun zeigen bestimmte Modelle einen Clip für einen neuen Film. BMW sagt, das sei gar keine Werbung.

spiegel.title: Migrationskrise in Ceuta: Sie schwammen über Leichen – und wollen es wieder versuchen
spiegel.description: Zehntausende schwammen nach Ceuta, viele ertranken. Mehr als zwei Dutzend Migranten berichten dem SPIEGEL, marokkanische Sicherheitskräfte hätten sie über die Grenze gedrängt. Eine Rekonstruktion der Ereignisse.

spiegel.title: Deutsche Bahn: Strecke Berlin–Hamburg wird nachts erneut gesperrt
spiegel.description: Erst seit wenigen Wochen rollen die Züge wieder regulär auf der Strecke zwischen Berlin und Hamburg. Für August und September sind nun weitere nächtliche Sperrungen wegen Restarbeiten und technischer Abnahmen vorgesehen.

spiegel.title: Trashformat »Villa der Versuchung«: Wo alles eine Ware ist, ist nichts wahr
spiegel.description: In der »Villa der Versuchung« müssen Promis sich alles kaufen, Zigaretten, ein Bett, Kleidung. Die Sendung spielt Gelüste des Einzelnen gegen die Gemeinschaft aus. Das Problem: Verzicht bringt Sympathien, Krawall den nächsten Job.

spiegel.title: Niederlande – Wassenaar: Großbrand an Dünen an der Nordseeküste
spiegel.description: Nahe einem Villenort in den Niederlanden ist ein Großbrand in den Dünen ausgebrochen. Die Feuerwehr brachte den Brand aber ebenso unter Kontrolle wie ein Feuer im Osten des Landes.

spiegel.title: Allgemeine Wehrpflicht: So könnte ein neuer Zivildienst aussehen
spiegel.description: Für den Fall einer Rückkehr zur Wehrpflicht bereitet die Bundesregierung eine Reaktivierung des Zivildienstes vor. Was bedeutet das für junge Menschen? Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten.

spiegel.title: Litauen: Grenzschützer entdecken Tunnel unter Zaun zu Belarus
spiegel.description: Litauische Grenzschützer stoßen erneut auf einen Tunnel an der Grenze zu Belarus. Die Behörden vermuten, dass der Gang für die illegale Schleusung von Migranten genutzt werden sollte, um Druck auf die EU auszuüben.

spiegel.title: Frankreich – Jean Pormanove: Bewährungsstrafen für Streamer nach Tod von Raphaël Graven
spiegel.description: Eine Gruppe französischer Streamer verdiente an Gewaltvideos. Ihr Opfer: Raphaël Graven alias Jean Pormanove. Der starb vergangenes Jahr vor laufender Kamera. Nun sind Urteile gefallen.

spiegel.title: Playmobil: Spielzeughersteller schreibt erneut Verlust in dreistelliger Millionenhöhe
spiegel.description: Playmobil schreibt erneut Verlust in dreistelliger Millionenhöhe, die Produktion des einstigen deutschen Vorzeigeunternehmens wandert ins Ausland. Getrieben wird die Krise auch von eklatantem Missmanagement.

spiegel.title: München: Vor Urteil im Prozess um Anschlag auf Verdi-Demonstration - wie geht es den Opfern?
spiegel.description: Farhad N. lenkte in München seinen Pkw in eine Ver.di-Demo, eine Frau und ihre Tochter starben. Nun will das Gericht das Urteil gegen ihn verkünden. Welche Bedeutung hat es für die überlebenden Opfer?

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Wassermangel in den Alpen, Lehren aus Ceuta, Gianni Infantino
spiegel.description: In den Alpen herrscht Wassermangel. Die EU macht sich mit ihrer Reaktion auf Ceuta angreifbar. Und: Gianni Infantino lädt zur Krisensitzung. Das ist die Lage am Mittwochabend.

spiegel.title: USA: Abdul El-Sayed gewinnt Vorwahl in Michigan
spiegel.description: Abdul El-Sayed wird beim Rennen um den Senatssitz in Michigan für die Demokraten antreten. Er setzt sich für eine staatliche Krankenversicherung und gegen Waffen für Israel ein. Donald Trump attackiert ihn schon.

spiegel.title: Mexiko: Influencer César Gastelum während Livestreamings auf offener Straße erschossen
spiegel.description: Sie kamen auf einem Motorrad und schossen: Zwei Männer haben in Mexiko den Influencer César Gastelum getötet, als der gerade sendete.

spiegel.title: »Letzte Verteidigungswelle«: Gericht stuft Gruppe als Terrorvereinigung ein
spiegel.description: Acht Neonazis im Alter von 14 bis 21 Jahren sollen Anschläge begangen und geplant haben. Das Oberlandesgericht Hamburg verurteilt sie wegen Mitgliedschaft in einer terroristischen Vereinigung. Ändert das etwas an ihrer Gesinnung?

spiegel.title: Ukraine: Olha Stefanischyna, Ex-Botschafterin in den USA, in Korruptionsfall angeklagt
spiegel.description: Bis vor Kurzem war Olha Stefanischyna Botschafterin der Ukraine in den USA. Nun ermittelt die ukrainische Justiz gegen sie. Laut Medienberichten wird ihr unrechtmäßige Bereicherung vorgeworfen.

observador.title: Metade dos africanos quer emigrar para a Europa
observador.description: Relatório do Afrobarometer ouviu cidadãos de 38 países. China mantém influência positiva; EUA perdem terreno. Angola é o único país onde a maioria não quer mais voz na ONU.

observador.title: 274 mil euros para requalificar posto da GNR no Algarve
observador.description: Câmara algarvia assinou consignação da obra na segunda-feira. Empreitada adjudicada à J.G. Benedito tem 100 dias de prazo e inclui pintura, reparações e melhoria de acessibilidades.

observador.title: Mourinho absolvido pelo TAD no caso Benfica-Porto
observador.description: O Tribunal Arbitral do Desporto absolveu o agora técnico do Real Madrid da suspensão de 11 dias e das coimas de 5.355 euros impostas pela FPF após o empate 2-2 em março.

observador.title: Festival Dunas de São Jacinto recebe GNR, Agir e Aurea
observador.description: O festival, de 21 a 23 de agosto, traz também o Aveiro Air Show, dezenas de aeronaves ultraleves e a estreia nacional do espetáculo noturno VOGUE.

observador.title: Ação contra indicadores de produtividade é "precipitada"
observador.description: A juíza-secretária do CSTAF defende que os novos Valores Processuais de Referência não vinculam a avaliação dos juízes administrativos e fiscais, ao contrário do que alega a ASJP.

observador.title: Farmácias de Bragança sem stock de óculos para o eclipse
observador.description: Farmácias e óticas de Bragança venderam mais de 1.800 óculos certificados ISO 12312-2. A cidade é o epicentro do eclipse total, visível a 100% em Rio de Onor e Guadramil.

observador.title: EUA pagam 87 mil milhões em reembolsos sobre taxas ilegais
observador.description: As tarifas anunciadas por Trump em abril de 2025 foram declaradas ilegais em fevereiro de 2026.   Estimam-se 166 mil milhões cobrados indevidamente.

observador.title: CNE remete para o MP boletins municipais do Seixal
observador.description: A Comissão Nacional de Eleições detetou indícios de crime nos boletins municipais de julho e agosto de 2025, por violação da neutralidade eleitoral. Paulo Silva (CDU) nega irregularidades.

observador.title: As notícias das 23h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Lousã investe 2,4 milhões em pavilhão multiusos
observador.description: O terreno de 17 mil metros quadrados permitirá criar uma infraestrutura multiusos para espetáculos, congressos e feiras, além de um parque de lazer, um centro de negócios e um espaço de cowork.

observador.title: Moçambique reforça assistência a 250 mil pessoas
observador.description: As autoridades vão reforçar a assistência alimentar em Sofala e pré-posicionar alimentos perante o risco de seca associado ao El Niño, que ameaça agravar a insegurança alimentar.

observador.title: Infantino is back: o novo plano para recuperar a hegemonia
observador.description: The Times dá conta da promessa de atribuição da final de 2030 a Marrocos em troca de apoio, entre várias manobras para voltar a ter o domínio. FIFA nega notícia. Silêncio da Arábia Saudita preocupa.

observador.title: Menos violência no desporto pelo segundo ano seguido
observador.description: Rodrigo Cavaleiro destacou dois anos consecutivos de descida de incidentes. A ministra Balseiro Lopes esteve presente na cerimónia de assinatura.

observador.title: 22h. Partidos não querem mais videovigilância no Parlamento
observador.description: Uma proposta feita por um grupo de trabalho com elementos da GNR e PSP. Ainda, Irão chegou a acordo com Omã sobre nova rota marítima no estreito de Ormuz.

observador.title: ETAR de Barcelos: concurso lançado com 35 milhões
observador.description: A obra, a instalar em Vila Frescainha São Pedro, tem prazo de execução de 910 dias e inclui tecnologias de ozonização, reutilização de água e produção de energia.

observador.title: Ucrânia ataca Amazon russa: "Até setembro, não sobra nada"
observador.description: Ucrânia diz que ataques contra a Wildberries servem para prejudicar economia russa e criam problemas à máquina de guerra russa. Diretora da empresa critica "ataques sem senso".

observador.title: Viúvas Negras. Esquema para lucrar com morte de soldados
observador.description: Um novo esquema de mulheres que casam com soldados para receber indemnizações de guerra. Ainda, Putin muda generais.

observador.title: Marco Silva: "Nada ficará decidido amanhã"
observador.description: Marco Silva não quis revelar já se efetuará alterações na formação inicial, mas com o mercado em curso e com a saída de António Silva, há decisões a serem tomadas. A primeira mão é disputada na Luz.

elpais.title: Marruecos procesa a 86 personas por organizar cruces irregulares en Ceuta y Melilla

elpais.description: La instructora solicita también datos sobre los operativos de rescate y los fallecidos

elpais.title: Penélope Cruz y Salma Hayek: la anécdota del maquillaje como prueba de una de las amistades más sólidas de Hollywood

elpais.description: La totalidad apenas durará unos minutos, por lo que se recomienda situarse dentro de la franja, utilizar gafas homologadas y evitar que hacer fotografías reste protagonismo a la experiencia

elpais.title: Washington y los Rodríguez inician las negociaciones para la transición venezolana con Machado al margen
elpais.description: Dinorah Figuera, apadrinada por Estados Unidos, lidera al equipo opositor que se sienta esta semana a negociar con el chavismo

elpais.description: El Gobierno argentino evita ofrecer disculpas por los agravios del presidente ultra a Lula

elpais.title: Irán insiste en mantener el control del estrecho de Ormuz mientras Trump amenaza con abrirlo por la fuerza
elpais.description: Teherán propone a Omán un sistema que le atribuiría la supervisión del tráfico y el cobro de tasas vinculadas a cuestiones de seguridad y el medio ambiente

elpais.title: Ola de indignación en Perú por una agresión sexual contra una cantante de cumbia
elpais.description: Los videos en los que la intérprete Naldy Saldaña aparece siendo sometida a tocamientos por el director musical de la orquesta La Bella Luz han escandalizado a la población peruana. La Fiscalía investiga el caso

republika.description: Il gigantismo dei tornei, i calendari senza tregua, racchette supersoniche e servizi a 200 all’ora: lo sport dei gesti bianchi è diventato un mestiere usurante. Così lo spagnolo rinuncia anche a Cincinnati e forse agli Us Open

nyt.title: Suspected Iran Cyberattacks on U.S. Water Supply Follow Years of Warnings and Neglect
nyt.description: Federal and state officials are racing to address an assault on the nation’s water supply that they believe is the work of Iranian hackers.

nyt.title: Trump Said Qatari Jet Was Destined for His Library. That May Change.
nyt.description: A White House official says no final decision has been made about which plane will go on display at the Trump presidential library. That leaves the fate of the Qatari jet unclear.

nyt.title: Helicopter Carrying Trump Flies Near Passenger Jet in Washington Airspace
nyt.description: Marine One, the helicopter that ferries the president, came within less than a mile of an Envoy Air flight on Tuesday, raising new concerns about air traffic control in the congested area.

nyt.title: Michigan Democrats Pick El-Sayed
nyt.description: Also, the Senate confirms a new C.D.C. director. Here’s the latest at the end of Wednesday.

nyt.title: El-Sayed’s Michigan Senate Primary Win Sets Up the Left’s Biggest Test of the Fall
nyt.description: Abdul El-Sayed’s Senate candidacy poses a critical challenge for Democrats’ ascendant progressive wing: Can an insurgent candidate, with unabashedly liberal positions, win a general election in a moderate state?

nyt.title: Bunny Dolls and Disturbing Allegations: Max Miller’s Strange CNN Interview
nyt.description: In a 23-minute appearance with the anchor Jake Tapper, the Ohio Republican made an unusual effort to rebut a multitude of allegations that have threatened his re-election bid.

nyt.title: Shri Thanedar Is Ousted by a Democratic Socialist in a Michigan House Primary
nyt.description: Representative Shri Thanedar is among a wave of Democratic incumbents in Congress whom primary voters have sent packing in a surge of anti-incumbent fervor this cycle.

nyt.title: C.I.A. Sets Up Secret Cuba Task Force as Trump Pressures Havana
nyt.description: The task force will allow the spy agency to quickly direct more financial, human and technical resources at the island, with the goal of creating fissures among the Cuban political elite.

nyt.title: Why Congress Wants a Closer U.S.-Israel Defense Partnership
nyt.description: A proposal making its way through Congress would integrate the U.S. and Israeli defense and intelligence apparatuses more tightly. Some worry that it is a bad idea.

nyt.title: Iran Says It Is Nearing Final Agreement With Oman on Strait of Hormuz
nyt.description: The agreement on an acceptable route for ships to pass through the strait would effectively ratify Tehran’s control over the crucial waterway.

nyt.title: Star Scholar Jason Arday Resigns From Cambridge
nyt.description: Jason Arday was hired by the University of Cambridge in 2023 as the youngest Black professor in its history. Doubt has since been cast on his academic qualifications and claims about his life.

nyt.title: Cambridge Professor Jason Arday’s Work Challenged Ahead of Book Launch
nyt.description: A knife-wielding masked man. A pig’s head outside his parents’ door. Running 30 marathons in 35 days. The Cambridge professor Jason Arday, accused of plagiarism, says he’s been through it all. Not everyone believes him.

nyt.title: U.S. Cuts Ties With Organ Donor Group After Reports of Abuses
nyt.description: The federal government is ending its contract with a Kentucky nonprofit that it says pressured medical workers to remove organs from patients who were getting better.

nyt.title: Lobga Rangzen, the Tibetan Activist Who Set Himself on Fire in Manhattan
nyt.description: No one doubted the intensity of Lobga Rangzen’s commitment to a Tibet free of Chinese control. But they were not prepared for what he did next.

nyt.title: Death Renews Scrutiny of Delaney Hall. Here’s What to Know.
nyt.description: The death of a Salvadoran immigrant at the federal detention center in Newark has raised questions about the conditions there.

nyt.title: ICE Threatens Sheriffs In Chicago and Minneapolis With Prosecution Over Access to Inmates
nyt.description: In a new tactic, federal immigration officials recently started saying they would criminally charge the elected county sheriffs in Minneapolis and Chicago.

nyt.title: How Malta Became a Tax Haven for Crocs and Other U.S. Companies
nyt.description: The Mediterranean archipelago is a hot destination for U.S. companies seeking to shield profits from income taxes.

nyt.title: Windy Weather Could Worsen Pacific Northwest Fires
nyt.description: Forecasters expect winds to pick up in eastern Washington and Oregon on Friday and Saturday, but not to be as strong as last weekend’s were.

npr.title: Ousted Bangladeshi leader vows to return from exile despite facing a death sentence

phys-org.title: We can help frogs beat a deadly disease. But can they still reproduce?

phys-org.description: Storm conditions capable of causing major coastal erosion at New Jersey's North Beach on Sandy Hook are occurring about twice as often as they did in 1979, according to Rutgers researchers. The finding offers new evidence that storm impacts are becoming more frequent along the Mid-Atlantic coast.

phys-org.title: Laser scanning may help prevent urban trees from falling
phys-org.description: For the first time, a group of biologists and engineers from the University of São Paulo (USP) in Brazil applied LiDAR (light detection and ranging) technology to investigate the health of trees and optimize pruning with the aim of reducing the risk of trees falling. This laser-sensing technology creates a "point cloud," a kind of 3D digital mold consisting of millions of coordinates that reproduces the plant's exact architecture in a computer.

phys-org.title: Attosecond X-ray method maps early electron motions that trigger chemical reactions
phys-org.description: All chemistry starts with a push from electrons. In the early moments of a chemical reaction, it's the movement of electrons that initiates the breaking of old chemical bonds and forging of new ones, transforming one molecule into another.

phys-org.title: 'Spooky' particles transit DC suburbs, a step toward a quantum network
phys-org.description: In early 2025, special signals wended their way through a fiber-optic highway strung above the streets and sidewalks of the Maryland suburbs. The arrival of those signals at their destination marks a significant step toward a long-held dream of building a "quantum network." Researchers believe that this emerging technology could someday link quantum devices in ways that supercharge scientific research, enable ultrasecure communications and boost the power of future quantum computers.

phys-org.title: Well-worn wins: Wild capuchin monkeys prefer stones with a proven track record of cracking nuts
phys-org.description: A new study provides experimental evidence that wild capuchin monkeys use more than just physical cues when selecting stone tools; they also rely on visible signs that a stone has previously been used for this purpose.

phys-org.title: A small molecular module helps time development of C. elegans
phys-org.description: For an animal to develop normally, cells must not only become the right types but also do so at the right time. In the worm C. elegans, the protein LIN28 has long been known as an important regulator of this timing: It keeps cells in a flexible state and delays their shift toward adult-like forms. In humans and other mammals, related LIN28 proteins have been associated with the timing of puberty.

phys-org.title: Genomic evidence suggests coral reefs may be rewriting their genetic future in real time
phys-org.description: The 2019 heat wave that struck Mo'orea—a volcanic island in French Polynesia—swept through its coral reefs like an invisible wildfire. Colorful, lively corals bleached into ghostly, chalk-white skeletons as soaring ocean temperatures triggered a mass mortality event (MME) that wiped out up to 80% of some local coral populations.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?

But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine

One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing

Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

proj-syn.title: The Right Way to Regulate AI
proj-syn.description: Governments tend to treat AI as a national-security challenge while devoting far less attention to its effects on education, health, labor markets, and the judiciary. Addressing AI’s societal risks requires institutions designed to recognize and respond to emerging threats before they become systemic failures.

proj-syn.title: Global Tax Reform Is the Key to a Fair AI Economy
proj-syn.description: The rise of AI has highlighted how the global tax system is ill-suited to capture the profits derived from such technology. While creating an equitable AI economy ultimately requires a durable and robust multilateral tax framework, digital-service taxes can serve as an important stepping stone to that outcome.

proj-syn.title: Aid’s Next Chapter
proj-syn.description: Wars, epidemics, displacement, and geopolitical competition will ensure that rich countries continue to spend money abroad, whether for humanitarian reasons or in pursuit of their own interests. The only question is what sort of aid system will emerge from the current retrenchment.

proj-syn.title: Peace With Iran Won’t Last Unless It Benefits Ordinary Iranians
proj-syn.description: A sustainable peace agreement between the United States and Iran will require more than military deterrence. Without financial sanctions relief that fuels job creation and generates real economic opportunities for ordinary Iranians, it will likely suffer the same fate as the 2015 nuclear deal.

proj-syn.title: Why Wealth Taxes Always Fail
proj-syn.description: A clear-eyed view of past experience shows that where wealth taxes have been tried, they have usually been abandoned—and for good reason. As policymakers in California, New York, France, and elsewhere revisit this old idea, they should heed the lessons of this history.

proj-syn.title: A New Paradigm for Global Health Financing
proj-syn.description: As aid flows decline, more countries are articulating a new vision in which health financing would build on national resources, answer to domestic priorities, and remain accountable to their own citizens. Such a change is long overdue, and it can be achieved by pursuing reforms in three areas.

proj-syn.title: The Triumph of India’s Cockroaches
proj-syn.description: The concessions secured by the "cockroach movement" amount to more than a triumph for prospective medical students or a brief political headache for the country's ruling party. They prove that even after years of centralization and institutional erosion, power remains with the people.

proj-syn.title: Zombie Monetarism
proj-syn.description: Three prominent economists, including a former Federal Reserve governor and adviser to US President Donald Trump, have just endorsed “soft monetarism” as a way to guide the Fed's approach to inflation. But the "quantity theory" of money failed for good reasons, and those reasons have not changed.

proj-syn.title: Taiwan Needs a New Deterrence Strategy
proj-syn.description: Emboldened by US President Donald Trump’s war in Iran, Chinese leaders have ramped up their gray-zone coercion against Taiwan in recent months. To avert a Chinese invasion, Taiwan must ensure that other democracies cannot function without it by providing them with more than just semiconductors.

proj-syn.title: What a Sino-American G2 Would Mean for Asian Security
proj-syn.description: The G2 concept that Donald Trump has lately been touting is a highly unstable proposition, which could make the emergence of a unipolar Asia more likely. Fortunately, Japan remains committed to advancing the far more effective “free and open Indo-Pacific” framework, with India as an indispensable partner.

proj-syn.title: Tearing Down the Currency Wall
proj-syn.description: Most of the world seems to misunderstand why global capital is not financing the developing world’s climate transition. The real problem lies in the structure of price formation, which policymakers can best address by focusing on three key priorities.

proj-syn.title: The Case for a Pay-Where-You-Play Tax System
proj-syn.description: The global tax system has repeatedly put corporate interests ahead of people and the planet by allowing multinationals to transfer profits to tax havens. If adopted, the proposed UN Framework Convention on International Tax Cooperation would overturn the century-old rules that make this possible.

proj-syn.title: The Canary in the AI Coal Mine
proj-syn.description: The greatest danger posed by AI is not the technology itself, but the race to deploy it before we know how to control it. The recent Hugging Face breach shows how seemingly minor human errors can be amplified by AI, underscoring the risks of treating safety as an afterthought.

proj-syn.title: The Painful Incompetence of the Indian State
proj-syn.description: India’s relatively weak state capacity has long hampered its development. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been promising to address the problem since he came to power in 2014, but his government’s emphasis on centralizing power and strengthening executive control has had the opposite effect.

proj-syn.title: This Time Could Be Different for Russia Sanctions
proj-syn.description: High inflation and interest rates are eating away at the foundations of the Russian economy and sapping its growth. By hitting its most important sectors, and its essential source of foreign hard cash, new US legislation would pile enormous pressure on the Kremlin just when it is urgently needed.

proj-syn.title: Africa’s Energy Curse Is a Political Choice
proj-syn.description: It is no secret why African countries with large fossil-fuel reserves nonetheless have failed to reduce extreme poverty or provide reliable electricity to all households. Those in power have made a conscious choice to privilege hard-currency export revenues, some of which then finance elite consumption rather than public investment.

proj-syn.title: The EU’s Incredible Shrinking Banking Sector
proj-syn.description: At the start of the millennium, all five of the largest European banks had a higher market capitalization than the largest US bank. What explains the fact that a quarter-century later, the largest US bank has a higher capitalization than all five top EU banks combined, and how can European policymakers address this dramatic reversal?

proj-syn.title: AI Must Enlarge the Economy, Not Divide It
proj-syn.description: To unlock AI’s full economic potential, we must steer it toward expansion. That requires replacing incentives that favor capital over labor with those that reward augmentation and investment in human capability.
